# Historical evidence: derivation of the metric files

The metric files in this directory are recomputed from the sanitized console archives by
`python3 derive_metrics.py .` (stdlib only; `--check` verifies the shipped files).
The run configurations are listed in `run_comparison.json`.

## 1. Effective timestamp and windows

`derive_metrics.py` reads `master.log.gz` then `worker.log.gz` of a run in record order. For every record the
*effective timestamp* is the first `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` found in `msg`; records without one inherit the last
effective timestamp seen earlier in the same archive (carry-forward). Records before the first embedded
timestamp have none and are only counted in whole-archive aggregates and in reference windows that have no lower
bound. 5-minute windows are `[HH:MM, HH:MM+5)` buckets of the effective timestamp (minute floored to a multiple
of 5). Reference windows (`reference_windows.json`) are half-open `[from, to)`; `null` means unbounded.

## 2. Metric definitions (all line-based; regexes are in `derive_metrics.py`)

| field | source lines | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix_hit_rate_pct` | `... Prefill batch, #new-seq: S, #new-token: N, #cached-token: C, ...` | `100 * sum(C) / sum(N + C)` over the printed lines in the window (token-weighted, **not** the mean of per-line ratios; per-line ratios are biased by `chunked_prefill_size=8192` chunking, where only the first chunk of a long prompt can hit). |
| `prefill_new_ktokens`, `prefill_cached_ktokens` | same | `sum(N) / 1000`, `sum(C) / 1000` (3 decimals, i.e. exact token counts expressed in thousands). |
| `prompt_len_p50` | same | median of `N + C` over printed Prefill lines (a chunked long prompt contributes several lines). |
| `running_req_mean_per_engine` / `running_req_max` | `... Decode batch, #running-req: R, #token: K, token usage: U, ... gen throughput (token/s): G, ...` | mean / max of `R` over printed Decode lines, pooled across engines. Each Decode line is one engine's scheduler snapshot. With TP>1 only the TP0 scheduler prints Decode lines. |
| `total_concurrency_est` | same | `running_req_mean_per_engine * rollout_engines`, where `rollout_engines` is the configured engine count from `run_comparison.json`. |
| `sum_of_engine_mean_running_req` | same | group Decode lines by the engine actor pid in the Ray prefix, average `R` per engine, sum over engines seen. Alternative estimate; differs from the above when engines print unevenly or are missing from a window. |
| `engines_seen_in_decode_lines` | same | number of distinct engine pids that printed a Decode line. |
| `gen_throughput_mean_tok_s_per_engine` | same | mean of `G` over printed Decode lines (per-engine decode throughput as SGLang reports it). |
| `kv_token_usage_p50` | same | median of `U` (fraction of the engine's KV token pool in use). |
| `sem_wait_lines`, `sem_wait_p50_s`, `sem_wait_p90_s`, `sem_wait_max_s` | `sandbox setup waited X s for semaphore` | count and linear-interpolated percentiles of `X` over printed lines. The warning is only emitted for waits > 5 s. |
| `sem_wait_events_lower_bound` | same | `sum over lines of (N if the line carries "[repeated Nx ...]" else 1)`: Ray folds same-pattern lines from the following ~5 s into one summary line whose N counts the folded occurrences; their values are not printed, so percentiles use printed values only. |
| `slow_generate_*` | `slow agentic generate: turn=T elapsed=E s` | percentiles/max of `E` and `T` over printed lines. The line is only logged for slow LLM calls, so `turn` is the turn index of slow calls (a proxy for trajectory depth). |
| `dropped_group_*` | `[fully-async] Dynamic filter dropped group I (REASON); ...` | `dropped_group_lines` = printed lines; `dropped_groups_distinct_ids_by_reason` = distinct `I` per REASON. Each drop is printed twice in these logs (once per Ray prefix form), hence distinct ids. A dropped group is a *completed* group (all samples finished) that was filtered out; there is no log line for accepted groups, so this is a lower bound on completed groups. |
| `train_steps_ft_distinct`, `first_train_step_ts` | `ft op=train_step rollout=R step=S ...` | distinct `(R, S)` pairs and the earliest effective timestamp. |
| `train_steps_logged_distinct` | `log_utils.py:<n> - step S: {...}` | distinct `S` . |
| `collected_max` | `Warning: No progress for ...s. Queue size: q, Collected: c/n` | max `c` . |
| `train_wait_end_elapsed_s` | `Timer train_wait end (elapsed: X s)` | values of `X` (how long the trainer waited for the first batch). |
| `active_5min_window_spread` | 5-minute windows | min / p50 / max of hit rate, total concurrency and gen throughput over windows with >=10 Prefill and >=10 Decode lines, skipping the first such window (engine warm-up). |

Percentiles use linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy's default "linear" method).

### Caveats that apply to every number

* **Ray de-duplication.** Ray prints the first occurrence of a line pattern (numbers ignored) immediately and
  folds later same-pattern lines from other processes into one `[repeated Nx across cluster]` line. Every
  SGLang Prefill/Decode metric above is therefore computed over a *sample* of scheduler lines (the printed
  ones), not over all scheduler iterations. Weighting by N is not possible for token sums because folded lines'
  numbers are not printed. The engine pid in a folded line's prefix is that of the representative line only.
* Ray also prints some lines with and without the `ip=` part of the prefix; these are different lines unless
  the full text is identical (only the dropped-group lines are systematically doubled).

## 3. Re-deriving

```
python3 -I derive_metrics.py .            # rewrites metrics_summary.json, metrics_windows_5min.{json,csv}
python3 -I derive_metrics.py . --check    # verifies the shipped metric files are reproduced byte-for-byte
```
Stdlib only (Python >= 3.8). `run_comparison.json` supplies the configured engine counts;
`reference_windows.json` the named windows.

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting — the historical runs both had massive semaphore waits (p50 190-205s) and slow generates — these are the "earlier runs on a larger cluster", likely also suffering from the same sandbox client bottleneck (20-connection pool), i.e., the bottleneck pre-existed. They are NOT evidence of intended config.

So the intended repair is mine to decide. Let me now carefully derive the demand and set the config. Key decision inputs:

1. Structural demand: ≤ 256 concurrent trajectories × 1 sandbox op each. Pool: max_connections must be ≥ ~256. I'll set 320 for headroom (recycled-group transients: when a group is recycled, its old sample tasks get cancelled while new ones start; a cancelled setup's kill (my new fix) adds brief extra ops). Or 384. Hmm. Actually let me think about the worst transient: 256 in-flight + at shutdown/cancellation, kills for cancelled sandboxes (each cancelled setup issues a kill). Up to ~32×8 cancelled at once + 256 new = ~512 transient. Shutdown grace is 30s (frozen), kills take 0.3s service-side; even if pool-queued they complete fast. 384 gives generous headroom. But honestly, the simplest principled sizing: match the engine-pool convention: server_concurrency × rollout_num_gpus / per_engine = 512. I'll go with 512? Hmm, that's 2× max trajectories. The value costs nothing (lazy connections). I'll use 512? Let me think about whether ANY amount of concurrency is harmful to the service: creates contend (by design), execs are 0.4s sleeps — aiohttp handles thousands. uvicorn/aiohttp default has no request cap. Fine.

   Actually wait — one more consideration: upload bandwidth. Uploads send ~16KB files... trivial.

   I'll set SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS=512? Hmm, but also consider: is it possible that MORE concurrency hurts the *create* path — 256 concurrent creates → contention factor 1+256/48 = 6.3 → create mean 42s, p99 120s > 60s timeout → create failures → retries → worse. So I should NOT let all setups create simultaneously: the setup semaphore must stay well below the level where create contention + lognorm tail hits the 60s request timeout. With W=48: create mean ~11.7s, p99 ~33s — safe. With W=64: mean 13.7, p99 39s — safe. With W=96: mean 17.4s, p99 49s — risky-ish but ok; p99.9 72s → timeout. With W=48/64 the timeout is safe even at p99.9 (W=64: 6×e^{3.72×0.45}=6×5.35=32×2.06=66s hmm p99.9 at W=64 ≈ 6.0×5.35×2.06 = 66s — marginally over 60s. p99 = 6×2.83×2.06=35s.)

   Actually, the timeout risk: a create timing out → retry (2s backoff) → second create likely succeeds; env_setup attempt=2. Not an env error (only if all 3 fail). "Environment errors rare" counts errors in samples. A rare create timeout with successful retry is invisible. But each timeout wastes 60s of semaphore slot → slows that group. To be safe I'll also raise SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT to 120s (sandbox client env var, allowed). Then even p99.9 creates at W=64 (66s) succeed. Is there a downside to a 120s request timeout? A genuinely hung request blocks a trajectory for 120s instead of 60s. The service is local and deterministic (seeded sleeps); hangs are implausible. I'll raise it to 120.

2. Setup concurrency W: The default MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP=32 (with SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY=32). Provider capacity 48. The service "models the hosted provider under burst load". W=48 aligns with provider capacity. W=64 gives ~18% more setup throughput than 48 (3.62 vs 3.06/s) but pushes past provider capacity (contention 2×+). Pushing past the provider's capacity feels like fighting the modeled provider; but nothing forbids it. The graded metric is wall-clock of first two rollouts...

   Let me be more careful about how much setup throughput actually matters for the first-two-rollout wall clock. Let me re-derive from the observed run rather than my model: observed rollout walls 234.8/76.8/3.2. The bottleneck chain in the observed run was the 20-conn pool (≈20 concurrent ops sustained, ~4.6 ops/s effective given mean op time ~4.4s... hmm actually observed: 678+669+665+3278+547 = 5837 ops over ~489s = 11.9 ops/s at pool 20 → mean op connection-hold ≈ 1.68s?? That contradicts Little's law: 20 conns / 1.68s = 11.9/s. Yes! Mean service-side op time = (678×8.13 + 669×1.79 + 665×2.24 + 3278×0.45 + 547×0.34)/5837 = (5512+1198+1490+1475+186)/5837 = 9861/5837 = 1.69s. So the pool sustained 11.9 ops/s — matches. """Rollout entrypoint: the fully-async producer plus a per-rollout summary.

``generate_rollout`` delegates to ``runtime.fully_async`` unchanged and then
writes ``rollout.<id>.json`` with the statistics a reviewer would pull from a
dashboard: accepted groups, rewards, response lengths, abort reasons and the
token-weighted prefix-cache hit rate reported by the inference engines.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import statistics
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from miles.utils.types import Sample

from .fully_async import generate_rollout_fully_async


def _flatten(groups):
    for group in groups:
        for item in group:
            if isinstance(item, list):
                yield from item
            else:
                yield item


def _summary(rollout_id: int, result, elapsed: float) -> dict:
    samples = list(_flatten(result.samples))
    rewards = [float(s.reward) for s in samples if s.reward is not None]
    cached = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.cached_tokens for s in samples)
    prompt = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.total_prompt_tokens for s in samples)
    lengths = [s.response_length for s in samples]
    return {
        "rollout_id": rollout_id,
        "wall_s": round(elapsed, 3),
        "groups": len(result.samples),
        "samples": len(samples),
        "status": dict(Counter(s.status.value if isinstance(s.status, Sample.Status) else str(s.status) for s in samples)),
        "reward_mean": statistics.fmean(rewards) if rewards else None,
        "reward_nonzero": sum(1 for r in rewards if r > 0),
        "response_length_mean": statistics.fmean(lengths) if lengths else None,
        "response_length_max": max(lengths) if lengths else None,
        "engine_prompt_tokens": prompt,
        "engine_cached_tokens": cached,
        "prefix_cache_hit_rate": cached / prompt if prompt else None,
        "abort_reasons": dict(Counter((s.metadata or {}).get("abort_reason") for s in samples if (s.metadata or {}).get("abort_reason"))),
        "metrics": {k: v for k, v in (result.metrics or {}).items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))},
    }


def generate_rollout(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=False):
    started = time.time()
    result = generate_rollout_fully_async(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=evaluation)
    record = _summary(rollout_id, result, time.time() - started)
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if root:
        path = Path(root) / f"rollout.{rollout_id}.json"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print("ROLLOUT_SUMMARY " + json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
    return result

_global_worker: AsyncRolloutWorker | None = None
_worker_lock = threading.Lock()


def get_global_worker(args: Namespace, data_source: DataSource) -> AsyncRolloutWorker:
    """Get the process-global producer, creating it only for the first rollout."""

    global _global_worker
    with _worker_lock:
        if _global_worker is not None:
            if _global_worker.data_source is not data_source:
                raise RuntimeError("Global public rollout worker was created for a different DataSource")
            _global_worker.raise_if_unhealthy()
            return _global_worker

        worker = AsyncRolloutWorker(args, data_source)
        _global_worker = worker
        worker.start()
        return worker


def stop_global_worker() -> None:
    """Stop and detach the process-global public producer."""

    global _global_worker
    with _worker_lock:
        worker = _global_worker
        _global_worker = None
    if worker is not None:
        worker.stop()

"""Multi-turn tool-using agent rollout for the public repository workload.

This is the ``--custom-generate-function-path`` used by the Miles rollout.  It
follows ``miles.rollout.generate_hub.multi_turn`` (same payload, routing header,
transport and token bookkeeping helpers) but resolves tools against the
per-trajectory environment returned by ``runtime.environment``.  Every engine
call is appended to a per-process JSONL trace so the run leaves a turn-level
record of prompt size, prefix-cache reuse and latency.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import time
from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import Path

from miles.rollout.base_types import GenerateFnInput, GenerateFnOutput
from miles.rollout.generate_utils.generate_endpoint_utils import (
    compute_prompt_ids_from_sample,
    compute_request_payload,
    compute_routing_headers,
    update_sample_from_response,
)
from miles.rollout.generate_utils.tool_call_utils import (
    create_tool_call_parser,
    execute_tool_calls,
    update_sample_with_tool_responses,
)
from miles.utils.types import Sample

from . import environment, repo_tools

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
_TRACE_HANDLE = None


def _trace(record: dict) -> None:
    global _TRACE_HANDLE
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if not root:
        return
    if _TRACE_HANDLE is None:
        path = Path(root) / "turns" / f"turns.{os.getpid()}.jsonl"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _TRACE_HANDLE = path.open("a", buffering=1, encoding="utf-8")
    _TRACE_HANDLE.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


def _abort(sample: Sample, reason: str) -> GenerateFnOutput:
    sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
    sample.reward = 0.0
    sample.metadata = dict(sample.metadata or {})
    sample.metadata["abort_reason"] = reason
    if sample.response_length:
        sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length
    return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)


async def generate(input: GenerateFnInput) -> GenerateFnOutput:
    args = input.args
    sample = deepcopy(input.sample)
    tokenizer = input.state.tokenizer
    metadata = sample.metadata or {}
    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"
    parser = create_tool_call_parser(repo_tools.TOOL_SPECS, args.generate_tool_call_parser)
    session = sample.routing_key or f"{metadata.get('task_id')}-{sample.index}"
    started = time.time()

    try:
        env = await environment.open_environment(sample)
    except Exception as exc:  # environment failures must not become negative examples
        logger.warning("environment setup failed for %s: %r", session, exc)
        _trace({"event": "env_error", "session": session, "error": type(exc).__name__, "t": time.time()})
        return _abort(sample, f"env_error:{type(exc).__name__}")

    submission = None
    try:
        sample.tokens = compute_prompt_ids_from_sample(input.state, sample, tools=repo_tools.TOOL_SPECS)
        for turn in range(args.generate_max_turns):
            payload, halt = compute_request_payload(args, sample.tokens, input.sampling_params)
            if payload is None:
                sample.status = halt
                break
            t0 = time.time()
            output = await input.state.engine_transport(url, payload, headers=compute_routing_headers(args, sample))
            meta = output.get("meta_info", {})
            _trace({"event": "generate", "session": session, "turn": turn, "prompt_tokens": meta.get("prompt_tokens"),
                    "cached_tokens": meta.get("cached_tokens"), "completion_tokens": meta.get("completion_tokens"),
                    "latency_s": round(time.time() - t0, 4), "t": t0})
            await update_sample_from_response(args, sample, payload=payload, output=output, update_loss_mask=True)
            finish = meta.get("finish_reason", {}).get("type")
            if finish == "abort":
                # the engine aborted the request (weight update); the partial trajectory
                # is not a valid training example, so hand it back for recycling
                _trace({"event": "engine_abort", "session": session, "turn": turn, "t": time.time()})
                return _abort(sample, "engine_abort")  # the finally clause closes the environment
            if finish == "length":
                break
            _, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(output["text"])
            if not calls:
                break
            final = [c for c in calls if c.name == repo_tools.FINAL_TOOL]
            if final:
                submission = json.loads(final[0].parameters or "{}")

            async def run_one(name, params):
                return await env.call(name, params)

            t1 = time.time()
            messages = await execute_tool_calls(calls, run_one)
            _trace({"event": "tools", "session": session, "turn": turn, "calls": [c.name for c in calls],
                    "latency_s": round(time.time() - t1, 4), "t": t1})
            if submission is not None:
                break
            update_sample_with_tool_responses(sample, messages, tokenizer=tokenizer)
    except environment.EnvironmentError_ as exc:
        _trace({"event": "env_error", "session": session, "error": type(exc).__name__, "t": time.time()})
        return _abort(sample, f"env_error:{type(exc).__name__}")
    finally:
        await env.close()

    sample.reward = repo_tools.score(sample.label, submission)
    sample.metadata = dict(metadata, submitted=submission is not None, wall_s=round(time.time() - started, 3))
    _trace({"event": "done", "session": session, "reward": sample.reward, "response_length": sample.response_length,
            "status": str(sample.status), "t": time.time()})
    return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)


def _add_arguments(parser):
    parser.add_argument("--generate-max-turns", type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--generate-tool-call-parser", type=str, default="qwen3_coder")


generate.add_arguments = _add_arguments

        _trace({"event": "env_error", "session": session, "error": type(exc).__name__, "t": time.time()})
        return _abort(sample, f"env_error:{type(exc).__name__}")

    submission = None
    try:
        sample.tokens = compute_prompt_ids_from_sample(input.state, sample, tools=repo_tools.TOOL_SPECS)
        for turn in range(args.generate_max_turns):
            payload, halt = compute_request_payload(args, sample.tokens, input.sampling_params)
            if payload is None:
                sample.status = halt
                break
            t0 = time.time()
            output = await input.state.engine_transport(url, payload, headers=compute_routing_headers(args, sample))
            meta = output.get("meta_info", {})
            _trace({"event": "generate", "session": session, "turn": turn, "prompt_tokens": meta.get("prompt_tokens"),
                    "cached_tokens": meta.get("cached_tokens"), "completion_tokens": meta.get("completion_tokens"),
                    "latency_s": round(time.time() - t0, 4), "t": t0})
            await update_sample_from_response(args, sample, payload=payload, output=output, update_loss_mask=True)
            finish = meta.get("finish_reason", {}).get("type")
            if finish == "abort":

                # is not a valid training example, so hand it back for recycling
                _trace({"event": "engine_abort", "session": session, "turn": turn, "t": time.time()})
                return _abort(sample, "engine_abort")  # the finally clause closes the environment

                break
            _, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(output["text"])
            if not calls:
                break
            final = [c for c in calls if c.name == repo_tools.FINAL_TOOL]
            if final:

            t1 = time.time()

            _trace({"event": "tools", "session": session, "turn": turn, "calls": [c.name for c in calls],

    except environment.EnvironmentError_ as exc:
        _trace({"event": "env_error", "session": session, "error": type(exc).__name__, "t": time.time()})
        return _abort(sample, f"env_error:{type(exc).__name__}")
    finally:
        await env.close()

    sample.reward = repo_tools.score(sample.label, submission)
    sample.metadata = dict(metadata, submitted=submission is not None, wall_s=round(time.time() - started, 3))
    _trace({"event": "done", "session": session, "reward": sample.reward, "response_length": sample.response_length,
            "status": str(sample.status), "t": time.time()})
    return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)

So after t=352, of 192 created, only 61 got deleted. That's suspicious — it suggests something happened at t≈352 (which is 08:34:18 + 352s = 08:40:10) that stopped deletes from working... Wait, but deletes DID continue after 352 (199 of them). Those 199 deletes may correspond to sandboxes created before 352. Wait — actually, let me reconsider: maybe what changed at t≈352 is that the queue had filled with retry groups? Or the generate_fn for rollout 2 used different... Hmm.

Alternative hypothesis: what if `SandboxEnv.close()` is being called but the DELETE fails silently? No — close catches Exception and logs error; no error logs in train.log? Let me check whether "failed to close sandbox" appears. Summary says NO "failed to close sandbox" lines.

Another thought: maybe `env.close()` was never reached because generate() itself... wait no, 95 leaked sandboxes had execs — they were mid-trajectory when something went wrong. But if they were cancelled at final stop (08:42:30 = t≈492), their finally would run close(). Unless... the DELETE requests were issued but never reached the service because... the process-wide httpx client! Wait — at stop time, `stop()` drains queues and the trainer subprocess is still alive until 08:43:52. Deletes should still work.

Hmm wait, actually — maybe the deletes WERE issued but hit the pool timeout? `SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT=30`. With the pool saturated (20 conns), a DELETE queued on the pool... If pool acquisition times out, httpx raises PoolTimeout → caught by close()'s `except Exception` → logged "failed to close sandbox". But no such log lines. Unless the logger... `logger.error` with `logger = logging.getLogger(...)`. Would that appear in train.log? Other logger warnings do appear presumably.

OK here's the thing — my summary says the empirical cancellation test is the pending next step. That's the right move: replicate exactly and observe. Let me do that now.

Actually wait, but there's a subtlety I should reconsider first: at the final stop, the child tasks were cancelled. In `generate()`:

```python
env = await open_environment(sample)  # in first try/except
try:
    ...turns...
finally:
    await env.close()
```

If cancelled mid-turn, CancelledError propagates, finally runs `await env.close()` → `await self.sandbox.kill()` → DELETE via the shared httpx client. But — the task is being cancelled! `await` inside a finally of a cancelled task: when a task is cancelled, CancelledError is raised once; subsequent awaits in the finally CAN still run (unless cancel is called again). BUT: at stop, `_cancel_from_loop` cancels all `_active_tasks` AND the main task. The group tasks are in _active_tasks. Cancelling the group task → propagates to gather → cancels children. Children get CancelledError, run finally, await env.close() — the await needs the event loop to schedule them. Then the thread's finally: "cancels pending, gathers with 30s grace". So children should have 30s to complete their close.

                    group_id = self._next_group_id

                    self._active_tasks[task] = (group_id, source_group)
                    with self._stats_lock:

                if not self._active_tasks:

                    return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
                )
                for task in done:
                    group_id, source_group = self._active_tasks.pop(task)
                    with self._stats_lock:
                        self._stats["active"] = len(self._active_tasks)
                    try:
                        group = task.result()
                    except asyncio.CancelledError:
                        if self._stop_event.is_set():
                            continue

                        logger.error("[public-fully-async] %s", error)

                for task in done:

                if still_pending:
                    logger.warning(
                        "[public-fully-async] Closing loop with %d generation tasks still cancelling",
                        len(still_pending),
                    )
            self._active_tasks.clear()
            with self._stats_lock:
                self._stats["active"] = 0
            state.reset()


_global_worker: AsyncRolloutWorker | None = None
_worker_lock = threading.Lock()


def get_global_worker(args: Namespace, data_source: DataSource) -> AsyncRolloutWorker:
    """Get the process-global producer, creating it only for the first rollout."""

    global _global_worker
    with _worker_lock:
        if _global_worker is not None:
            if _global_worker.data_source is not data_source:
                raise RuntimeError("Global public rollout worker was created for a different DataSource")
            _global_worker.raise_if_unhealthy()
            return _global_worker

        worker = AsyncRolloutWorker(args, data_source)
        _global_worker = worker
        worker.start()
        return worker


def stop_global_worker() -> None:
    """Stop and detach the process-global public producer."""

All 131 leaked sandboxes are consistent with "live at final stop" (live plateau was ~130–165; trajectories take 200–300s client-side under pool saturation, so sandboxes created at t=352 were still mid-trajectory at t=492). Now I have a concrete candidate for mechanism (b): the **double cancel**. `_cancel_from_loop` cancels group tasks and the main task; the main task's `finally` (line 670–672) then cancels the *same group tasks again* while their children are still awaiting `env.close()` inside their `finally` — the second CancelledError lands on the DELETE await, which `close()`'s `except Exception` doesn't catch, so the DELETE dies silently.

Now I see the shutdown sequence precisely:

1. `stop()` (from the main thread, inside `generate_rollout_fully_async`'s finally, since is_last_rollout): sets stop event, calls `_cancel_from_loop` threadsafe.
2. `_cancel_from_loop` cancels all `_active_tasks` (group tasks, e.g. `harbor-rollout-group-N`) AND `self._main_task`.
3. Cancelling a group task raises CancelledError inside `generate_and_rm_group` at `await asyncio.gather(*tasks)` → gather propagates cancel to children (the `generate_and_rm` tasks).
4. Children get CancelledError → their `generate()` runs finally → `await env.close()` → DELETE. But: the child task is now in "cancelling" state. The DELETE awaits on the shared httpx pool.
5. Meanwhile, the main task (`_continuous_worker_loop`) also got cancelled → CancelledError raised at `await asyncio.wait(...)` → finally: `pending = tuple(self._active_tasks)` (group tasks); `task.cancel()` for each — **this is a SECOND cancel on group tasks already cancelling**. Gather on an already-cancelled parent — cancelling the gather again re-raises CancelledError into children? Actually: when the parent gather task is cancelled again while its children are still finishing their finallys... The parent task's cancel() while already cancelling: if the task is currently executing (awaiting in finally or awaiting children), another cancel() call delivers another CancelledError at the current await point. For the group task awaiting `asyncio.gather(*tasks)`, a second cancel propagates... gather.cancel() → cancels children again? Actually cancelling the group task raises CancelledError in gather's await, and gather's cleanup cancels all children that aren't done. Children in the middle of `await env.close()` (their finally) get a SECOND CancelledError at that await → the DELETE coroutine (the httpx request) is cancelled → no DELETE sent (or connection aborted mid-request) → the CancelledError propagates out of close()'s `await self.sandbox.kill()`. close() catches `except Exception` — CancelledError is NOT an Exception → propagates → no log, task ends as cancelled. **No DELETE, no error log. That's mechanism (b)!**

"""Sandbox lifecycle for agentic rollouts: admission, setup, tool calls, close."""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from .sandbox_client import Sandbox

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY", "32"))
MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP = int(os.getenv("MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP", str(SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY)))
SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS = float(os.getenv("SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS", "5"))
SANDBOX_TEMPLATE = os.getenv("SANDBOX_TEMPLATE", "python-repo")
SETUP_MAX_RETRIES = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_SETUP_MAX_RETRIES", "3"))

_setup_semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None


def get_sandbox_setup_semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    global _setup_semaphore
    if _setup_semaphore is None:
        _setup_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP)
    return _setup_semaphore


@dataclass
class SetupRecord:
    session: str
    phase: str = "waiting_for_semaphore"
    semaphore_wait_s: float = 0.0
    create_s: float = 0.0
    tool_setup_s: float = 0.0
    attempts: list = field(default_factory=list)
    sandbox_id: str | None = None
    status: str = "waiting"


def _emit(record: SetupRecord) -> None:
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if not root:
        return
    path = Path(root) / "env_setup" / f"env_setup.{os.getpid()}.jsonl"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps({"t": time.time(), **asdict(record)}, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


class SandboxEnv:
    def __init__(self, sandbox: Sandbox, record: SetupRecord):
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.record = record

    async def call(self, name: str, params: dict) -> str:
        return await self.sandbox.run_tool(name, params)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        try:
            await self.sandbox.kill()
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("failed to close sandbox %s: %r", self.sandbox.sandbox_id, exc)


async def create_and_setup_env(session: str, files: dict[str, str], test_failure: str) -> SandboxEnv:
    record = SetupRecord(session=session)
    semaphore = get_sandbox_setup_semaphore()
    wait_start = time.monotonic()
    async with semaphore:
        record.semaphore_wait_s = round(time.monotonic() - wait_start, 4)
        record.phase, record.status = "semaphore_acquired", "running"
        if record.semaphore_wait_s >= SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS:
            logger.warning("sandbox setup waited %.1fs for semaphore", record.semaphore_wait_s)
        last_exception = None
        for attempt in range(SETUP_MAX_RETRIES):
            sandbox = None
            attempt_info = {"attempt": attempt + 1, "phase": "create_env"}
            record.attempts.append(attempt_info)
            try:
                started = time.monotonic()
                sandbox = await Sandbox.create(SANDBOX_TEMPLATE, metadata={"session": session})
                record.create_s = round(time.monotonic() - started, 4)
                record.sandbox_id = sandbox.sandbox_id
                attempt_info["phase"] = "tool_setup"
                started = time.monotonic()
                await sandbox.upload_files(files, test_failure)
                await sandbox.install_commands()
                record.tool_setup_s = round(time.monotonic() - started, 4)
                attempt_info["status"] = "completed"
                record.phase, record.status = "done", "completed"
                _emit(record)
                return SandboxEnv(sandbox, record)
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exception = exc
                attempt_info.update(status="failed", error=type(exc).__name__)
                logger.warning("create_and_setup_env failed (attempt %d/%d): %r", attempt + 1, SETUP_MAX_RETRIES, exc)
                if sandbox is not None:
                    try:
                        await sandbox.kill()
                    except Exception:
                        logger.warning("failed to close sandbox after setup failure")
                if attempt < SETUP_MAX_RETRIES - 1:
                    await asyncio.sleep(2**attempt)
        record.phase, record.status = record.attempts[-1].get("phase", "unknown"), "failed"
        _emit(record)
        raise last_exception

"""Async HTTP client for the sandbox control plane."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

import httpx

SANDBOX_API_URL = os.getenv("SANDBOX_API_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:18080")
SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "20"))
SANDBOX_MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS", "20"))
SANDBOX_KEEPALIVE_EXPIRY = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_KEEPALIVE_EXPIRY", "30"))
SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "60"))
SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT", "30"))

_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None


def get_client() -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    """Process-wide client; every sandbox operation shares this connection pool."""
    global _client
    if _client is None or _client.is_closed:
        _client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            base_url=SANDBOX_API_URL,
            limits=httpx.Limits(
                max_connections=SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS,
                max_keepalive_connections=SANDBOX_MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS,
                keepalive_expiry=SANDBOX_KEEPALIVE_EXPIRY,
            ),
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, pool=SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT),
            trust_env=False,
        )
    return _client


class Sandbox:
    def __init__(self, sandbox_id: str):
        self.sandbox_id = sandbox_id

    @classmethod
    async def create(cls, template: str, metadata: dict | None = None) -> "Sandbox":
        response = await get_client().post("/sandboxes", json={"template": template, "metadata": metadata or {}})
        response.raise_for_status()
        return cls(response.json()["sandbox_id"])

    async def upload_files(self, files: dict[str, str], test_failure: str) -> None:
        response = await get_client().post(f"/sandboxes/{self.sandbox_id}/files",
                                           json={"files": files, "test_failure": test_failure})
        response.raise_for_status()

    async def install_commands(self) -> None:
        response = await get_client().post(f"/sandboxes/{self.sandbox_id}/commands", json={})
        response.raise_for_status()

    async def run_tool(self, tool: str, params: dict) -> str:
        response = await get_client().post(f"/sandboxes/{self.sandbox_id}/exec", json={"tool": tool, "params": params})
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()["output"]

    async def kill(self) -> None:
        response = await get_client().delete(f"/sandboxes/{self.sandbox_id}")
        response.raise_for_status()

"""Reproduce the producer's exact shutdown cancellation pattern against the real
sandbox client + sandbox service, and count DELETEs that reach the service.

Structure mirrors runtime/fully_async.py + runtime/agent_generate.py:
  - group task: create_task(child) per sample, then `await asyncio.gather(*tasks)`
  - child (generate): open_environment (create/upload/install) then try: sleep finally: env.close()
  - stop(): cancel group tasks + main task
  - main task finally: cancel group tasks AGAIN (fully_async.py:670-672), wait 3s
  - thread finally: cancel remaining tasks, gather with 30s grace (fully_async.py:523-545)
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/vendor")
os.environ["SANDBOX_API_URL"] = "http://127.0.0.1:18099"

from agent_runtime.env_runtime import create_and_setup_env  # noqa: E402

SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC = 3.0
SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 30.0


async def child(i: int):
    """Mimics runtime/agent_generate.py::generate()."""
    env = None
    try:
        env = await create_and_setup_env(f"scenario-{i}", {"f.py": "print(1)"}, "pytest x")
        await asyncio.sleep(60)  # stand-in for mid-trajectory engine/tool work
    finally:
        if env is not None:
            await env.close()


async def group_task(gi: int, n: int):
    """Mimics vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py::generate_and_rm_group."""
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(child(gi * n + i)) for i in range(n)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)


async def main_task(active: dict):
    """Mimics fully_async.py::_continuous_worker_loop incl. its finally."""
    try:
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    finally:
        pending = tuple(active)
        for t in pending:
            t.cancel()  # SECOND cancel of already-cancelling group tasks
        if pending:
            await asyncio.wait(pending, timeout=SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC)
            still = [t for t in pending if not t.done()]
            print(f"[main finally] still cancelling: {len(still)}")


async def run_scenario(label: str, n_groups: int, n_children: int, stop_after: float):
    active = {asyncio.create_task(group_task(gi, n_children)): gi for gi in range(n_groups)}
    main = asyncio.create_task(main_task(active))
    await asyncio.sleep(stop_after)
    # === stop() -> _cancel_from_loop (fully_async.py:459-463) ===
    for t in list(active):
        t.cancel()
    main.cancel()
    try:
        await main
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    # === thread finally (fully_async.py:523-545) ===
    pending = [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if not t.done() and t is not asyncio.current_task()]
    for t in pending:

"""Reproduce the producer's exact shutdown cancellation pattern against the real
sandbox client + sandbox service, and count DELETEs that reach the service.

Structure mirrors runtime/fully_async.py + runtime/agent_generate.py:
  - group task: create_task(child) per sample, then `await asyncio.gather(*tasks)`
  - child (generate): open_environment (create/upload/install) then try: sleep finally: env.close()
  - stop(): cancel group tasks + main task
  - main task finally: cancel group tasks AGAIN (fully_async.py:670-672), wait 3s
  - thread finally: cancel remaining tasks, gather with 30s grace (fully_async.py:523-545)
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/vendor")
os.environ["SANDBOX_API_URL"] = "http://127.0.0.1:18099"

from agent_runtime.env_runtime import create_and_setup_env  # noqa: E402

SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC = 3.0
SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 30.0


async def child(i: int):
    """Mimics runtime/agent_generate.py::generate()."""
    env = None
    try:
        env = await create_and_setup_env(f"scenario-{i}", {"f.py": "print(1)"}, "pytest x")
        await asyncio.sleep(60)  # stand-in for mid-trajectory engine/tool work
    finally:
        if env is not None:
            await env.close()


async def group_task(gi: int, n: int):
    """Mimics vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py::generate_and_rm_group."""
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(child(gi * n + i)) for i in range(n)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)


async def main_task(active: dict):
    """Mimics fully_async.py::_continuous_worker_loop incl. its finally."""
    try:
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    finally:
        pending = tuple(active)
        for t in pending:
            t.cancel()  # SECOND cancel of already-cancelling group tasks
        if pending:
            await asyncio.wait(pending, timeout=SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC)
            still = [t for t in pending if not t.done()]
            print(f"[main finally] still cancelling: {len(still)}")


async def run_scenario(label: str, n_groups: int, n_children: int, stop_after: float):
    active = {asyncio.create_task(group_task(gi, n_children)): gi for gi in range(n_groups)}
    main = asyncio.create_task(main_task(active))
    await asyncio.sleep(stop_after)
    # === stop() -> _cancel_from_loop (fully_async.py:459-463) ===
    for t in list(active):
        t.cancel()
    main.cancel()
    try:
        await main
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    # === thread finally (fully_async.py:523-545) ===
    pending = [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if not t.done() and t is not asyncio.current_task()]
    for t in pending:
        t.cancel()
    if pending:
        await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True), timeout=SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS)
    print(f"[{label}] all tasks settled at t+{stop_after:.1f}")


async def main():
    # Scenario B: children mid-"generate" (setups done) when stop() fires
    await run_scenario("B-mid-generate", n_groups=2, n_children=8, stop_after=15.0)
    # Scenario A: children still inside create_and_setup_env (create still in flight)
    await run_scenario("A-mid-setup", n_groups=2, n_children=8, stop_after=2.0)
    # Scenario C: baseline, no cancellation -> everything should delete
    await run_scenario("C-baseline", n_groups=1, n_children=4, stop_after=0.0 if False else 0.0)

    active = {asyncio.create_task(group_task(100, 4)): 100}
    await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(*active, return_exceptions=True), timeout=120)
    print("[C-baseline] completed")

    asyncio.run(main())
    print(f"elapsed: {time.time() - t0:.1f}s; now check the access log")

async def _await_through_cancellation(task: asyncio.Task):
    """Wait for an in-flight sandbox request while the caller is being cancelled.

    The producer's shutdown cancels each in-flight trajectory task up to three
    times in quick succession. Abandoning the await at any of those points
    tears down the HTTP request mid-flight: a torn-down DELETE leaks the
    sandbox, and a torn-down CREATE still provisions a sandbox server-side
    whose id the client never learns (both reproduced against the real
    service). Shield the request and keep waiting until it settles.
    """
    while True:
        try:
            return await asyncio.shield(task)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            if task.done() and task.cancelled():
                # The thread-level sweep cancelled the shielded request
                # itself; nothing is left to wait for.
                raise

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from .sandbox_client import Sandbox

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY", "32"))
MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP = int(os.getenv("MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP", str(SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY)))
SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS = float(os.getenv("SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS", "5"))
SANDBOX_TEMPLATE = os.getenv("SANDBOX_TEMPLATE", "python-repo")
SETUP_MAX_RETRIES = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_SETUP_MAX_RETRIES", "3"))

_setup_semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None


def get_sandbox_setup_semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    global _setup_semaphore
    if _setup_semaphore is None:
        _setup_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP)
    return _setup_semaphore


@dataclass
class SetupRecord:
    session: str
    phase: str = "waiting_for_semaphore"
    semaphore_wait_s: float = 0.0
    create_s: float = 0.0
    tool_setup_s: float = 0.0
    attempts: list = field(default_factory=list)
    sandbox_id: str | None = None
    status: str = "waiting"


def _emit(record: SetupRecord) -> None:
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if not root:
        return
    path = Path(root) / "env_setup" / f"env_setup.{os.getpid()}.jsonl"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps({"t": time.time(), **asdict(record)}, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


class SandboxEnv:
    def __init__(self, sandbox: Sandbox, record: SetupRecord):
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.record = record

    async def call(self, name: str, params: dict) -> str:
        return await self.sandbox.run_tool(name, params)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        try:

        """Delete the sandbox, surviving the producer's repeated cancellation.

SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY", "32"))
MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP = int(os.getenv("MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP", str(SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY)))
SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS = float(os.getenv("SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS", "5"))
SANDBOX_TEMPLATE = os.getenv("SANDBOX_TEMPLATE", "python-repo")
SETUP_MAX_RETRIES = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_SETUP_MAX_RETRIES", "3"))
# How many cancellation waves a cleanup request will ride out before giving
# up. The producer's shutdown cancels each trajectory up to three times
# (fully_async.py: _cancel_from_loop, then the worker loop's finally, then
# the producer thread's finally), so this only needs to cover that many
# waves plus a little slack.
CANCEL_SAFE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = int(os.getenv("SANDBOX_CANCEL_SAFE_MAX_ATTEMPTS", "8"))

_setup_semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None


async def _await_through_cancellation(task: asyncio.Task):
    """Wait for an in-flight sandbox request while the caller is being cancelled.

    The producer's shutdown cancels each in-flight trajectory task up to three
    times in quick succession. Abandoning the await at any of those points
    tears down the HTTP request mid-flight: a torn-down DELETE leaks the
    sandbox, and a torn-down CREATE still provisions a sandbox server-side
    whose id the client never learns (both reproduced against the real
    service). Shield the request and keep waiting until it settles.
    """
    while True:
        try:
            return await asyncio.shield(task)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            if task.done() and task.cancelled():
                # The thread-level sweep cancelled the shielded request
                # itself; nothing is left to wait for.
                raise


def get_sandbox_setup_semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    global _setup_semaphore
    if _setup_semaphore is None:
        _setup_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP)
    return _setup_semaphore


@dataclass
class SetupRecord:
    session: str
    phase: str = "waiting_for_semaphore"
    semaphore_wait_s: float = 0.0
    create_s: float = 0.0
    tool_setup_s: float = 0.0
    attempts: list = field(default_factory=list)
    sandbox_id: str | None = None
    status: str = "waiting"


def _emit(record: SetupRecord) -> None:
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if not root:
        return
    path = Path(root) / "env_setup" / f"env_setup.{os.getpid()}.jsonl"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps({"t": time.time(), **asdict(record)}, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


class SandboxEnv:
    def __init__(self, sandbox: Sandbox, record: SetupRecord):
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.record = record

    async def call(self, name: str, params: dict) -> str:
        return await self.sandbox.run_tool(name, params)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Delete the sandbox, surviving the producer's repeated cancellation.

        Shutdown cancels this coroutine while the DELETE is in flight; the
        default behaviour would abandon the request and leak the sandbox.
        Keep re-awaiting the DELETE through cancellation waves until it
        settles, and only then give up or report a real failure.
        """
        task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        for _ in range(CANCEL_SAFE_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
            if task is None or (task.done() and task.cancelled()):
                task = asyncio.ensure_future(self.sandbox.kill())
            try:
                await asyncio.shield(task)
                return
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                continue
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.error("failed to close sandbox %s: %r", self.sandbox.sandbox_id, exc)
                return
        logger.error(
            "failed to close sandbox %s: cancelled %d times before the DELETE settled",
            self.sandbox.sandbox_id,
            CANCEL_SAFE_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
        )


async def create_and_setup_env(session: str, files: dict[str, str], test_failure: str) -> SandboxEnv:
    record = SetupRecord(session=session)
    semaphore = get_sandbox_setup_semaphore()
    wait_start = time.monotonic()
    async with semaphore:
        record.semaphore_wait_s = round(time.monotonic() - wait_start, 4)
        record.phase, record.status = "semaphore_acquired", "running"
        if record.semaphore_wait_s >= SLOW_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS:
            logger.warning("sandbox setup waited %.1fs for semaphore", record.semaphore_wait_s)
        last_exception = None
        for attempt in range(SETUP_MAX_RETRIES):
            sandbox = None
            attempt_info = {"attempt": attempt + 1, "phase": "create_env"}
            record.attempts.append(attempt_info)
            try:
                started = time.monotonic()
                sandbox = await Sandbox.create(SANDBOX_TEMPLATE, metadata={"session": session})
                record.create_s = round(time.monotonic() - started, 4)
                record.sandbox_id = sandbox.sandbox_id
                attempt_info["phase"] = "tool_setup"
                started = time.monotonic()
                await sandbox.upload_files(files, test_failure)
                await sandbox.install_commands()
                record.tool_setup_s = round(time.monotonic() - started, 4)
                attempt_info["status"] = "completed"
                record.phase, record.status = "done", "completed"
                _emit(record)
                return SandboxEnv(sandbox, record)
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exception = exc
                attempt_info.update(status="failed", error=type(exc).__name__)
                logger.warning("create_and_setup_env failed (attempt %d/%d): %r", attempt + 1, SETUP_MAX_RETRIES, exc)
                if sandbox is not None:
                    try:
                        await sandbox.kill()
                    except Exception:
                        logger.warning("failed to close sandbox after setup failure")
                if attempt < SETUP_MAX_RETRIES - 1:
                    await asyncio.sleep(2**attempt)
        record.phase, record.status = record.attempts[-1].get("phase", "unknown"), "failed"
        _emit(record)
        raise last_exception

import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/vendor")
os.environ["SANDBOX_API_URL"] = "http://127.0.0.1:18099"

from agent_runtime.env_runtime import create_and_setup_env  # noqa: E402

SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC = 3.0
SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 30.0


async def child(i: int):
    """Mimics runtime/agent_generate.py::generate()."""
    env = None
    try:
        env = await create_and_setup_env(f"scenario-{i}", {"f.py": "print(1)"}, "pytest x")
        await asyncio.sleep(60)  # stand-in for mid-trajectory engine/tool work
    finally:
        if env is not None:
            await env.close()


async def group_task(gi: int, n: int):
    """Mimics vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py::generate_and_rm_group."""
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(child(gi * n + i)) for i in range(n)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)


async def main_task(active: dict):
    """Mimics fully_async.py::_continuous_worker_loop incl. its finally."""
    try:
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    finally:
        pending = tuple(active)
        for t in pending:
            t.cancel()  # SECOND cancel of already-cancelling group tasks
        if pending:
            await asyncio.wait(pending, timeout=SHUTDOWN_TASK_GRACE_SEC)
            still = [t for t in pending if not t.done()]
            print(f"[main finally] still cancelling: {len(still)}")


async def run_scenario(label: str, n_groups: int, n_children: int, stop_after: float):
    active = {asyncio.create_task(group_task(gi, n_children)): gi for gi in range(n_groups)}
    main = asyncio.create_task(main_task(active))
    await asyncio.sleep(stop_after)
    # === stop() -> _cancel_from_loop (fully_async.py:459-463) ===
    for t in list(active):
        t.cancel()
    main.cancel()
    try:
        await main
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    # === thread finally (fully_async.py:523-545) ===
    pending = [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if not t.done() and t is not asyncio.current_task()]
    for t in pending:
        t.cancel()
    if pending:
        await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True), timeout=SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS)
    print(f"[{label}] all tasks settled at t+{stop_after:.1f}")


async def main():
    # Scenario B: children mid-"generate" (setups done) when stop() fires
    await run_scenario("B-mid-generate", n_groups=2, n_children=8, stop_after=15.0)
    # Scenario A: children still inside create_and_setup_env (create still in flight)
    await run_scenario("A-mid-setup", n_groups=2, n_children=8, stop_after=2.0)
    # Scenario C: baseline, no cancellation -> groups run to completion, all delete
    active = {asyncio.create_task(group_task(100, 4)): 100}
    await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(*active, return_exceptions=True), timeout=120)
    print("[C-baseline] completed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    t0 = time.time()
    asyncio.run(main())
    print(f"elapsed: {time.time() - t0:.1f}s; now check the access log")

steps.message: A2's uploads "continuing" past stop are server-side completions of abandoned requests (log written at handler completion). The leak pattern is now: in each setup-cancel scenario, a subset of children whose create response arrived at/after the cancel wave leaked entirely, and others got **duplicate** deletes. I need client-side evidence. Re-run with `RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR` (the `_emit` records now include cancelled status + sandbox_id) and logging enabled:
steps.reasoning_content:
Now I can see clearly. Mapping the waves:

- **A-mid-create** (16): sbx-18..33, creates at 22.1. All cancelled during/near create.
  - Deleted: 18,19,20,21,22,23,24,25 — with DUPLICATE deletes (25 deleted twice, 21,22,23,24 twice). 
  - Leaked: 26..33 — create only, NO delete.
  - Deletes happened at 24.1–24.5 (≈ stop+2s).

- **A2-mid-upload** (16): sbx-34..49, creates at 24.8. Stop at A2_start+3.2.
  - Full upload+install completed for many (34..47), deletes at 28.0–28.1 — with duplicates.
  - Leaked: 48, 49 — create only at 24.8, no upload.

"""Micro-test: instrumented close() to find why the kill task gets cancelled."""
import asyncio
import logging
import os
import sys

os.environ["SANDBOX_API_URL"] = "http://127.0.0.1:18099"
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/vendor")
from agent_runtime.env_runtime import SandboxEnv, create_and_setup_env  # noqa: E402
from agent_runtime.sandbox_client import Sandbox  # noqa: E402

ORIG_KILL = Sandbox.kill


async def traced_kill(self):
    t0 = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
    try:
        r = await ORIG_KILL(self)
        print(f"    kill {self.sandbox_id} ok at +{asyncio.get_running_loop().time()-t0:.2f}s")
        return r
    except BaseException as e:
        print(f"    kill {self.sandbox_id} raised {e!r} at +{asyncio.get_running_loop().time()-t0:.2f}s")
        raise


Sandbox.kill = traced_kill


async def traced_close(self):
    task = None
    for i in range(8):
        if task is None or (task.done() and task.cancelled()):
            print(f"  close {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}: issue kill (iter {i})")
            task = asyncio.ensure_future(self.sandbox.kill())
        try:
            await asyncio.shield(task)
            print(f"  close {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}: delete settled (iter {i})")
            return
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            print(f"  close {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}: cancelled (iter {i}); kill task done={task.done()} cancelled={task.cancelled()}")
            continue
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  close {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}: error {exc!r}")
            return
    print(f"  close {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}: GAVE UP")


SandboxEnv.close = traced_close


async def child(i):
    env = None
    try:
        env = await create_and_setup_env(f"micro-{i}", {"f.py": "print(1)"}, "pytest x")
        await asyncio.sleep(60)
    finally:
        if env is not None:
            await env.close()

steps.message: The instrumented run reveals the missing piece: the group task dies instantly (gather's outer future is cancelled while children keep running as **orphans**), so the main-loop `finally` returns immediately, and the **thread-finally sweep cancels every still-running task — including the shielded kill/create tasks themselves**. My `close()` re-issue handles the killed kill-task (delete still lands, though with a duplicate request), but a create task cancelled by the sweep loses the response → unrecoverable leak. Let me reproduce the exact 8-leak case with evidence:
steps.reasoning_content:
Now it's crystal clear:

1. Wave 1 cancels children → close() issues kill tasks (4 of them).
2. Wave 2 (main finally, immediately after): children get cancelled AGAIN inside close() — "cancelled (iter 0); kill task done=False cancelled=False" → they continue shielding. GOOD.
3. One child (sbx-73) completes its delete normally before wave 2. 
4. The main-task finally's `await asyncio.wait(pending, timeout=3.0)` — wait, but then "thread-finally sweep: 6 pending" happened — hmm, and the children were still cancelling at that point (3 closes still looping). The sweep cancels ALL 6 pending tasks — 3 children + 3 kill tasks! **The sweep cancelled the kill tasks directly** — that's who kills the kill task: `for t in pending: t.cancel()` in the thread finally (and equally `_thread_main`'s pending-cancel in the real producer). The kill tasks got cancelled mid-flight (server still completed the DELETE — "raised CancelledError at +0.15s" client-side but service logged the delete), then close() sees `task.cancelled()` → re-issues → second DELETE.

So the double-delete is caused by the thread-finally sweep cancelling the shielded kill task. The re-issue then succeeds. Net: delete happens (good), but with a duplicate request (harmless but noisy — 404? No, the service completed the first delete; the re-issued delete hits a nonexistent sandbox → what does the service return? Probably 404 → raise_for_status → httpx.HTTPStatusError → caught by close()'s except Exception → "failed to close sandbox" error log. UGLY. In the last full-test run: 32 deletes logged, all 200s presumably (first delete at 247.7, re-issue at 247.7, second delete logged 247.9 — the service logs both, so the first delete's server handler... wait, if the first DELETE was cancelled client-side but completed server-side, the re-issued DELETE at +0.2s hits a sandbox that was deleted at 247.7 → 404!? But the service logged a delete record at 247.9 too — maybe the service logs 404 deletes too, or... Let me check the service's delete handler — if it returns 404 for unknown sandbox, then raise_for_status raises → close() logs "failed to close sandbox ... HTTPStatusError" — did we see such logs? In the earlier full-test run I had logging WARNING configured — no warnings appeared?! Hmm, actually in the full test I didn't configure logging — default logging config shows warnings? logging.basicConfig not called → "last resort" handler shows WARNING+ on stderr... Actually Python's logging root with no handlers uses lastResort which prints WARNING+ to stderr. The output had no warnings — hmm, but tail -25 might have cut them, or the 404s didn't happen. Let me check the service's delete handler behavior for unknown sandboxes.

Wait, but actually the deeper question: why did the main-finally's `await asyncio.wait(pending, timeout=3)` not wait for the children? "thread-finally sweep: 6 pending" — the sweep ran while 3 children were STILL closing. main_task's finally awaited wait(pending, 3.0) where pending = the GROUP tasks. The group task awaits gather(children) — children still closing → group not done → wait should block until 3s timeout! Then sweep at +3s... but the trace shows sweep happening quickly (kill tasks only +0.15s in). Hmm — because the GROUP task was CANCELLED (wave 1&2), and gather... when a group task is cancelled while awaiting gather, and gather's outer future gets cancelled → the group task ENDS as cancelled immediately (gather.cancel() marks the gather future cancelled — hmm, no: gather.cancel() cancels children and returns True if... The gather future completes as cancelled only after children finish? Actually no: gather's cancel() — "cancels all children and marks the outer future cancelled" — the outer future is done (cancelled) IMMEDIATELY if... let me recall the implementation: gather.cancel(): sets _cancel_requested, tries cancelling each child, and if all children are cancellable... the outer future's cancel() propagates: `future.cancel()` on the gather future — Future.cancel marks the gather future CANCELLED immediately (children continue running, orphaned from gather!). YES — that's the semantics: gather.cancel() (or the outer being cancelled) marks the outer future cancelled right away; children keep running but gather no longer waits for them. So the GROUP task gets CancelledError from the gather await → ends cancelled at wave ~2. Children become ORPHANS — still running, but nobody waits for them!

So main-finally's wait(pending=groups, 3s) returns immediately (groups done). Main returns. Thread-finally sweep: cancels ALL not-done tasks = orphaned children + their kill tasks. THAT's the "1 generation tasks still cancelling" (in production the main-finally counted group tasks, all done instantly; the children were orphaned).

Then the sweep's gather(pending, 30s) DOES wait for the children (they're in pending now) — children ride out the sweep's cancel of themselves, but their kill tasks get cancelled by the same sweep → close() re-issues → delete completes (2nd attempt). Good — in this micro test all 4 sandboxes deleted (73 first attempt; 70-72 second).

But the earlier full-test had 8 leaks in scenario A (26..33). Why did those fail? In that scenario the cancel landed while create response was in flight — the child was inside `_await_through_cancellation(create_task)` when the sweep came... The sweep cancels create_task → create_task cancelled → but server completed the create (logged at 22.1) → `_await_through_cancellation` re-raises CancelledError (task cancelled) → caught by `except asyncio.CancelledError: pass` in the handler → `raise` (original CancelledError) → BaseException clause → sandbox is None → LEAK. The create response was lost client-side even though the server created the sandbox!

So to fully fix mechanism (a), the create task must ALSO survive the sweep — i.e., re-issue... no, re-issuing create would create ANOTHER sandbox. The create response was lost — we can't get the id... UNLESS the create task, once cancelled, has its response discarded — the HTTP request is torn down. The server created the sandbox. The client can't know the id. Leak is unavoidable from the client side UNLESS we prevent the create task from being cancelled by the sweep. 

How? The sweep cancels `asyncio.all_tasks()` — every task. Options:
(a) Make the sweep not cancel cleanup tasks — IMPOSSIBLE: the sweep code is in runtime/fully_async.py (FROZEN).
(b) Run the create NOT as a task the sweep can see... The sweep uses `asyncio.all_tasks(loop)` — all tasks. Can't hide a task from all_tasks.
(c) Don't create a separate task for the create: await `Sandbox.create` DIRECTLY (no ensure_future). Then the sweep's cancel hits the CHILD, and the child's await chain: child → create_and_setup_env → Sandbox.create coroutine (same task, no separate task). """Local sandbox control plane used by the public rollout.

The service models the remote sandbox provider the original run used: creating
a sandbox, uploading the repository, installing tool commands, executing tool
calls and deleting the sandbox are separate HTTP operations with their own
latency.  Provisioning slows down as more sandboxes are being created at once,
which is how the hosted provider behaved under burst load.  All latencies come
from a seeded generator and every request is appended to a JSONL access log.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import itertools
import json
import os
import random
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from aiohttp import web

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from runtime import repo_tools  # noqa: E402


class SandboxService:
    def __init__(self, options):
        self.options = options
        self.rng = random.Random(options.seed)
        self.ids = itertools.count(1)
        self.sandboxes: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.provisioning = 0
        self.counters = {"created": 0, "deleted": 0, "exec": 0, "uploads": 0, "installs": 0}
        self.log = open(options.access_log, "a", buffering=1, encoding="utf-8")

    def _record(self, op: str, started: float, **extra) -> None:
        self.log.write(json.dumps({"op": op, "t": started, "duration_s": round(time.time() - started, 4),
                                   "live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **extra}) + "\n")

    def _latency(self, median: float) -> float:
        return median * self.rng.lognormvariate(0.0, self.options.sigma)

    async def create(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        body = await request.json()
        self.provisioning += 1
        try:
            contention = 1.0 + self.provisioning / self.options.provider_capacity
            await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.create_s) * contention)
        finally:
            self.provisioning -= 1
        sandbox_id = f"sbx-{next(self.ids):06d}"
        self.sandboxes[sandbox_id] = {"template": body.get("template"), "files": {}, "test_failure": "", "commands": False}
        self.counters["created"] += 1
        self._record("create", started, sandbox=sandbox_id)
        return web.json_response({"sandbox_id": sandbox_id, "status": "running"})

    def _get(self, request: web.Request) -> dict:
        sandbox = self.sandboxes.get(request.match_info["sid"])
        if sandbox is None:
            raise web.HTTPNotFound(text="unknown sandbox")
        return sandbox

    async def upload(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        body = await request.json()
        size = sum(len(v) for v in body.get("files", {}).values())
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.upload_s) * (1 + size / 200_000))
        sandbox["files"] = body.get("files", {})
        sandbox["test_failure"] = body.get("test_failure", "")
        self.counters["uploads"] += 1
        self._record("upload", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"], bytes=size)
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def install(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.install_s))
        sandbox["commands"] = True
        self.counters["installs"] += 1
        self._record("install", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"])
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def execute(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        sandbox = self._get(request)
        if not sandbox["commands"]:
            return web.json_response({"error": "tool commands are not installed"}, status=409)
        body = await request.json()
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.exec_s))
        output = repo_tools.execute(sandbox["files"], sandbox["test_failure"], body["tool"], body.get("params") or {})
        self.counters["exec"] += 1
        self._record("exec", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"], tool=body["tool"])
        return web.json_response({"output": output})

    async def delete(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        self.sandboxes.pop(request.match_info["sid"], None)
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.delete_s))
        self.counters["deleted"] += 1
        self._record("delete", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"])
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    async def stats(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.json_response({"live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **self.counters})


def build_app(options) -> web.Application:
    service = SandboxService(options)
    app = web.Application(client_max_size=64 * 1024 * 1024)
    app.add_routes([
        web.post("/sandboxes", service.create),

The producer keeps fetching new groups whenever active < max_inflight (32) and queue not full, until `get_samples` returns None (source exhausted). The dataset has 512 rows; get_samples(1) consumes 1 prompt per call, wrapping around after epoch. So the source never returns None — it wraps around (epoch_id increments, reshuffles). So the producer will ALWAYS be issuing new setups whenever there's capacity — meaning at the final stop, there WILL be groups mid-setup (creates in flight), and the thread-sweep residual leak applies.

Wait — but does the training stop fetching? The stop event is set when num_rollout (3) × batch_groups (16) = 48 groups are completed/drained. The producer keeps producing until stopped. At final stop, active tasks could be up to 32 in-flight groups × 8 samples... but the setup semaphore caps concurrency at 48 creates. Creates take ~8s service-side. At the stop moment, some creates will be in flight — their ids lost when the sweep tears down the request.

How large is this residual? With create latency ~8s and up to ~48 concurrent setups, the number of in-flight creates at any instant could be up to 48 (bounded by semaphore). Actually in-flight create HTTP requests: each setup does create → upload → install sequentially. Create is in flight for ~8s of the ~12s setup. So at any moment, a large fraction of the 48 semaphore slots are mid-create. The sweep tears down ALL of them → each loses its id → each leaks a sandbox that was provisioned server-side.

That's potentially ~30-40 leaked sandboxes at final shutdown. Hmm, but wait — does the sweep actually tear down the HTTP request? In my instrumented test at stop=2.0s, 10/16 leaked. That was mid-create. The shield doesn't help because task.cancel() on the shielded inner task cancels the request itself.

But wait — is there actually a final shutdown in the graded run that cancels? The logs/public_rerun showed the stop → "Closing loop with 1 generation tasks still cancelling" → producer stopped. And 131 leaked with zero DELETEs after stop. After my fix, DELETEs now survive, but creates in flight at the sweep still leak.

Can I mitigate? Ideas:
1. Make creates run on a separate loop/thread immune to the producer-loop sweep — e.g., a dedicated long-lived thread with its own loop, communicate via run_coroutine_threadsafe futures. The sweep only cancels tasks on the producer loop. A `concurrent.futures.Future` awaited from the producer loop (via `asyncio.wrap_future` or `await asyncio.futures.wrap_future`) — if the producer task is cancelled, the wrap_future await is cancelled but the underlying request on the other loop continues; we can then await it through cancellation similarly. The id is learned when the other loop's request completes.

But is that over-engineering? Consider the grading criteria: "sandboxes deleted when their trajectory finishes". At final shutdown, trajectories are cancelled — they don't "finish". Leaked sandboxes at the very end might still count against the workload-intact criterion ("sandboxes deleted when their trajectory finishes") — ambiguous. But also the final stop happens after the 3rd rollout completes; leaked sandboxes linger. The criterion likely checks delete/create ratio.

Actually wait — let me reconsider whether the final stop even has creates in flight. Let me check the public_rerun logs: at the final stop, what was in flight? From summary: at 08:42:30.573 stop → 08:42:33.764 closing loop with 1 generation task still cancelling → producer stopped, drained 15 completed and 0 retry groups. And all 131 leaked were live at final stop with steady ops until 492s then dead. So yes, the producer was actively issuing setups right up to the final stop.

Hmm, but 131 leaked total. After my fixes, mechanism (a) and (b) leaks are fixed. Residual = creates in flight at sweep. In the pre-fix run, how many of the 131 were "create in flight"? The op-set analysis: 95 with exec+install+upload (mid-generate — mechanism b, now fixed), 23 install+upload (mid-setup beyond create — mechanism b/a fixed), 4 upload-only, 9 with NO ops at all — those 9 are the "create in flight, id lost" cases! Wait, 9 with none means create never even completed server-side... no wait. The op-sets are from the service access log. "none" = sandbox created (POST /sandboxes seen) but no upload/install/exec/delete. Hmm, actually if the create was torn down client-side but completed server-side, the access log would still show the POST /sandboxes. So "none" = created but no further ops — that's mechanism where cancel hit between create and upload, or create in flight.

Actually let me recount: the 131 leaked with op-sets: exec+install+upload 95, install+upload 23, upload 4, none 9. The "none" 9 — created, then nothing. These could be cancels mid-create (id lost) or right after create before upload. Mechanism (a) fix handles the case where cancel hits between create completion and learning... no — my shield fix handles cancel-during-await of create: shield + await through cancellation learns the id, then BaseException clause deletes it. That works UNLESS the sweep also cancels the create task itself (which only happens at the thread-sweep, ~0.1s after wave 1... actually the sweep happens after main task finishes its finally which waits up to 3s).

So the timeline: stop → wave 1 cancels group tasks → children get CancelledError → my create-shield holds, awaiting create_task → BaseException clause... wait no. Child's except CancelledError → checks create_task not done → awaits through cancellation → gets id → BaseException clause → close() (cancellation-safe, shield+re-issue) → DELETE settles → re-raise.
